classification.difficultyReason: Apply one half-turn about the origin to four points, including the fixed origin.

content.prompt: Mark the given points on a number plane. Find their images under a rotation of $180^\circ$ anticlockwise about the origin $O$. Draw each image point and write down its coordinates.

answer.worked: A half-turn places the image on the opposite side of the origin at the same distance. Plot $A(2,-1)$ and $A'(-2,1)$; the origin is the midpoint of $AA'$.
A half-turn places the image on the opposite side of the origin at the same distance. Plot $B(2,1)$ and $B'(-2,-1)$; the origin is the midpoint of $BB'$.
Plot $C$ at the origin. The centre of rotation is fixed, so $C'$ coincides with $C$ at $(0,0)$.
Plot $D$ two units above the origin. After a half-turn, $D'$ is two units below the origin, at $(0,-2)$.

spec.description: Complete common coordinate plane showing the original points and their half-turn images. Original and image points use the same black markers and distinct editable labels.
